In alignment with the Trusted Workforce (TW) 2.0 framework, the legacy system of periodic reinvestigations is replaced by Continuous Vetting (CV). All contractor personnel shall be enrolled in and subject to CV protocols once their initial background investigation is favorably adjudicated. Enrollment and monitoring will be managed through the Defense Information System for Security (DISS), the National Background Investigation Services (NBIS), or successor Government systems of record. INTRODUCTION The Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP) supports force readiness and quality of life by providing policies, programs, resources, and outreach that advance the well-being of service members, including the National Guard, Reserve, and Coast Guard; their families, survivors, and other eligible members of the military community. Title 10, U.S. Code, Chapter 88, Subchapter I, Military Family Programs, is a statutory driver for Online Learning Systems and MilLife Learning. It requires online resources that provide comprehensive information to members of the Armed Forces and their families regarding available benefits and services, including contact information for obtaining specific assistance. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) establishes the requirements for online training support services that are timely, accurate, accessible, user-focused, mission- relevant, and compliant with applicable laws, regulations, policies, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and data protection requirements. C- 2. OVERVIEW OF THE REQUIREMENT High Level Scope Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used across the public service and has the potential to support improved service delivery, productivity and innovation. Its use also creates important responsibilities for public bodies and their staff in relation to responsible use, data protection, information security, transparency, accountability and human oversight. The Local Government Management Agency (LGMA), on behalf of the local government sector, seeks to engage a suitably qualified provider to develop a suite of short, accessible online training modules providing baseline AI literacy and awareness training for local authority staff. ip_data_security.text: (LGMA), on behalf of the local government sector, seeks to engage a suitably qualified provider to develop a suite of short, accessible online training modules providing baseline AI literacy and awareness training for local authority staff. The purpose of the training is to establish a consistent baseline level of AI literacy across the sector and provide staff with the knowledge required to understand AI, recognise the responsibilities associated with its use, and use AI appropriately and responsibly within a public-service environment. The training suite will cover seven topics: AI fundamentals; Responsible AI; Public service obligations; Data protection considerations; Information security considerations; Human oversight; and Awareness of the EU AI Act. The training is intended as baseline awareness training for staff generally and is not intended to provide specialist, technical or role-specific AI training. This reflects the current sector approach of providing a universal AI literacy baseline separately from practical tool-specific enablement. The successful tenderer will work with the LGMA and its nominated representatives to agree the structure, learning objectives and detailed content of each module before development commences.
